Independent phase and Floquet algebra, strict inequalities, and unimodality of the forcing function
correctness.rationale: The additive y-update forces x phases ±p; the two first-coordinate equations are equivalent to q²+p²/4=1−1/β and αcos p=βqp². Thus β≤1 is impossible; otherwise 0<p<P=2√(1−1/β)≤√2 and q>0. Direct differentiation gives the stated phase matrices; their determinant product is (B−1)²−(k+3t)² and the return trace is 2−2B−(k+t)², giving det(I−M)=B²−4kt−8t². For β≥3/2 and p≤1, tan p>p makes the normalized determinant strictly less than (p²−1)(p²+8/3)≤0, forcing a real multiplier >1. For p>1, tan p≥p+p³/3 yields the stated trace estimate: the bracket exceeds 49/24−2 and P²−p²>0, so tr M<−2. This forces a multiplier of modulus >1, not necessarily a positive real one. Below 3/2 the terminal amplitude branch limits to (5−4β)I; strict spectral stability and the intermediate value theorem give sinks at every sufficiently small positive forcing. Independently, the forcing function h(p)=βp²√(1−1/β−p²/4)/cos p has derivative with the sign of P²−H(p), where H=p²+p²/(2+p tan p). H′=p[12−p²+9p tan p+(p tan p)²]/(2+p tan p)²>0, so h has one maximum. At β=17/10, P>1 and h(1)≥(17/10)√(11/68)>1/10, proving exactly two illustrative cycles since h tends to zero at both ends.
residual_risks: No claim of a full forcing-dependent stability diagram below 3/2, nor coverage above β=2, global basins, or higher periods.

value.rationale: The orbit census does not distinguish sinks from strictly unstable orbits. This sharp gain threshold answers that question uniformly at arbitrary positive forcing on the excluded side, including the equality endpoint, and constructs actual sinks for all sufficiently small forcing on the other side. It supplies qualitative information about a studied system without overstating it as a full stability diagram.
residual_risks: Only local exponential attraction and primitive period two are addressed.
